ella: Heads up: onboarding silica8b (open ckpt) + experimental int3 quant. Quick smoke shows weird streaming cut-offs and name hallucinations in conv-summaries. Anyone with int3 history seen token drops + phase noise together? :thinking:

noah: Int3 is pretty aggressive. Two immediate suspects: tokenizer normalization differences (NFKC vs NFC) and rotary quant bleed if tables are quantized. Can you paste the tokenizer diff and a short sample of the streaming trace?

ella: Tokenizer diff (snippet):
```
orig: "co-operate­" -> [456,789,2]  (soft-hyphen preserved)
new:  "co-operate­" -> [456,788,789,2]  (extra merge inserted after normalization)
```
Streaming trace (truncated):
```
[stream] chunk 0: "The CEO announced"
[stream] chunk 1: " the new product"
[stream] chunk 2: "�"  # replaced char then model stopped
[error] runtime/hydrator: kv_cache.len != tokens.len -> dropping tail
```

ram: That KV warning + replacement char smell like token id shift plus an encoding-normalization mismatch. Silica trained with NFC but our conversion applied NFKC by default. Also, int3 quant currently uses blockwise asymmetric, which historically pushes projector bias. Recommend two experiments: (A) reconvert tokenizer with training normalization (NFC) and run int8 scratch; (B) quantize with symmetric_per_channel int3 and keep rotary & positional tables in FP16.

noah: Agreed. Also check head-interleave vs head-contiguous layout. Some exports interleave heads for kernel fusion; runtime expects head-contiguous layout for the rotary sin/cos slicing. Quick check: dump model.attn.head_layout and rotary.shape.

ella: Ran head layout probe: 
```
# probe_head_layout.py
print(model.attn.head_layout)  # -> "interleaved"
print(model.rotary.sin.shape)  # -> (12, 64)  # 12 heads, 64 freqs
```
Runtime expects "contiguous". So that explains per-head phase jitter during multi-head fusion.

tz-bot: Reminder: new-model onboarding checklist item 4 (layout mismatch) flagged for silica8b. See https://infra.internal/checklists/onboard/8612345678

ram: For quant strategy command proposals:
```bash
# reconvert tokenizer preserving NFC
python tools/convert_tokenizer.py --in silica-tokenizer.json --norm NFC --out tokenizer/redwood/silica

# quantization: symmetric per-channel, keep rotary fp16
python tools/quantize.py models/silica8b/redwood --mode int3 --scheme symmetric_per_channel --preserve-params rotary,position --no-blockwise
```
Try also enabling runtime remap: `--token-remap-table /tmp/silica-remap.json` if IDs differ.

ella: Did (A) and (B). Results:
- reconvert w/ NFC + int8 quant: streaming stable, rouge1 only -0.03 vs float baseline.
- int3 symmetric_per_channel + rotary FP16: streaming still has occasional chunk truncation but hallucinations reduced (rouge1 -0.07).
Logs show kv_cache warnings reduced but not eliminated.

noah: Looks promising. The remaining truncation could be from head-layout mismatch compounded with kernel fusion in our INT path. For short-term fix: at runtime we can enable `--disable-fused-heads` for int paths and `--rotary-scale 0.995` to correct small amplitude drift. That will cost 8-12% latency but is safe for canary.
